title: Step navigation posture is linear by default with free-step as the elicited alternative
context: Wizards divide on how much freedom the operator has to jump between steps. A linear posture forbids advancing until the current step is Completed and disables backward jumps to steps whose prerequisites the domain says must be Completed first (an application with a payment step gated on shipping details, say). A free posture lets the operator pick any step at any time and computes the completion states independently. Neither is wrong; the choice is a per-project posture driven by the domain the wizard serves. GOV.UK Design System publishes the step-by-step navigation pattern as the widely-adopted linear model.
decision: Adopt linear as the recommended default. The shipped task-list disables rows whose [data-step-state] is Cannot start yet by rendering them as spans without an href. Projects that want free navigation elicit ADR-2501 to the free branch and every row renders as an anchor. recommendedDefault is true because linear is the safer starting posture for a domain the shelf blueprint does not know; elicited is true because the switch is a real per-project answer.
consequences: Projects on the default get a linear wizard out of the box with no configuration; the task-list refuses out-of-order entry and the operator walks the manifest in order. Projects electing free get an unconstrained task-list at the price of surfacing every prerequisite the domain implies through the manifest and the copy. All three step-indicator shapes (ADR-2503) render on both branches; the difference is only the click-through on rows whose prerequisites are unfinished.

alternativesConsidered.name: Free-step as the shipped default
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship free navigation everywhere and rely on per-step validation to catch out-of-order entries.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses the affordance the domain often needs (a payment step should not be reachable before shipping details); reads as more forgiving but pushes the domain rule into copy rather than into the surface.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two-step wizard with no task-list
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship no task-list at all and rely on Back and Next.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses the completion overview and the ARIA progressbar; a wizard with three or more steps benefits materially from the task-list surface.
